summary: This resolution expresses House support for designating May 3-9, 2026 as Wildfire Preparedness Week and for related public education, early warning systems, evacuation planning, and efforts to reduce human-caused ignitions.

scores.thoughts: The resolution is a symbolic expression of support for Wildfire Preparedness Week and related education efforts. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or directives related to federal budgets, appropriations, or spending levels of any kind.
The bill makes no reference to taxes, tax policy, revenue measures, or any changes to the tax code.
While the preamble notes health impacts of wildfire smoke, the resolution itself does not address healthcare policy, coverage, delivery systems, or funding.
No connection whatsoever to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation has zero relation to immigration, border policy, or immigrant protections.
No mention or implication regarding reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces operations.

The resolution references wildfire statistics, smoke health effects, and preventative measures including vegetation management, but it is a non-binding awareness resolution that neither expands environmental protections nor limits regulations. Any link is purely incidental.
No provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net policies.
The measure supports public education initiatives on fire safety but does not engage with K-12 schooling, federal education funding, school choice, or education policy.
Completely unrelated to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No bearing on sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains nothing about trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization.
No fiscal policy implications or references to deficits or debt reduction.
Zero connection to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The resolution does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
Unrelated to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No provisions concerning technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
The bill does not engage with labor rights, union power, or workplace regulations.
No discussion of religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
